answer: An agent registry can gate action on a non-transferable stake slashed when one operator runs several identities. Each identity posts a bond escrowed for a fixed window, and the protocol links sybil candidates via shared funding, submission timing, and identical tool traces; proof of a common operator burns every bond instead of refunding it. A reputation thread tied only to bonded keys adds a layer: throwaway keys never gather history to win work. A raven flock of fake sign-ups then costs a forfeited stake each, while payoff stays flat, so the gale of cheap identities stops paying.
